title: Splitting a w-local cover identifying local rings
statement: Let $R,S$ be commutative rings and $g:R\to S$ a faithfully flat ring map [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map]. Assume both spectra are w-local [def-weil-pbc-w-local], and $\pi_0(\operatorname{Spec}R)$ is extremally disconnected (the closure of every open subset is open). Let $I\subseteq R$ be an ideal such that $V(I)$ is the closed-point subset of $\operatorname{Spec}R$ and $V(IS)$ is the closed-point subset of $\operatorname{Spec}S$. Suppose that for every prime $q\subset S$ the canonical map $R_{g^{-1}(q)}\to S_q$ is an isomorphism [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Then there is a ring map $s:S\to R$ with $s\circ g=\mathrm{id}_R$.

source.place: Tag 09AZ, lemma-w-local-extremally-disconnected, implication (3) to (1), specialized to a w-local target with closed points V(IS)

proof.text: Let h: ConnectedComponents(Spec S) → ConnectedComponents(Spec R) be the map induced by g. By faithful flatness and [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-surjective-spectrum], Spec S → Spec R is surjective; the induced map h is continuous, and it is surjective because a preimage of a point in each connected component lies in a connected component mapping into that component. By [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-component-ring-pullback], both component spaces are compact Hausdorff, while the target is extremally disconnected by hypothesis. The section node therefore supplies a continuous section ρ of h.

source.place: Tag 09AZ, proof of (3) => (1), paragraph beginning “π₀(Spec S) → π₀(Spec R) admits a continuous section”

proof.text: Put T = range(ρ). Since the component space of Spec S is compact Hausdorff, T is closed. The identity h ∘ ρ = id makes h restricted to T bijective onto ConnectedComponents(Spec R). If q is a closed point of Spec S, then q ∈ V(IS), so IS ⊆ q and I ⊆ g⁻¹(q); hence g⁻¹(q) ∈ V(I), the closed-point subset of Spec R. Thus the required closed-point contraction property holds.

source.place: Tag 09AZ, proof of (3) => (1), paragraphs on closed points and the range of the section

proof.text: Apply the closed-component retraction lemma to g, the closed-point contraction property, and T. Its stalk-bijectivity hypothesis is exactly the assumed canonical isomorphisms R_{g⁻¹(q)} ≅ S_q, and its component-surjectivity and injectivity hypotheses are supplied by the preceding section. We obtain a ring map s:S→R with s∘g=id_R.
